item.title: Incarico post-doc: Robotics for agriculture (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IINF-05 Sistemi di elaborazione delle informazioni

item.title: Incarico post-doc: CFD analysis of an air system for thermal storage with PCM (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-04 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/ICHI-01 Sistemi, metodi e tecnologie dell'ingegneria chimica e di processo

The research project focuses on the fluid-dynamic and thermal study and optimization of a Thermal Energy Storage (TES) system based on Phase Change Materials (PCM), using air as the heat transfer fluid. The objective is to develop and validate transient Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation models to analyze the charging (melting) and discharging (solidification) processes of the PCM. The study will evaluate different heat exchanger geometries and operating air parameters to overcome the low thermal conductivity limitation of PCMs, thereby maximizing heat transfer efficiency.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Pica Code IPD-2026-062 NEAT: A Multi-Camera Platform for Neuroinclusive Ergonomic Assessment and Task Allocation (Univ. MODENA e R. E.)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 13:00
Institution: Univ. MODENA e R. E., Reggio Emilia
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IIND-05 Impianti industriali meccanici

The successful candidate will conduct experimental campaigns for the acquisition of motion data in industrial and laboratory environments using a multi-camera RGB-D system based on Orbbec Femto Bolt cameras, a commercial multi-camera Vicon Vero 2.2 IR system, and a 31-sensor Synertial inertial suit. The candidate will analyse the collected data using the CLI, Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation, OWAS, RULA and REBA indices, define criteria to support task allocation and sequencing based on ergonomic risk, and assess the technical, economic and environmental sustainability of the proposed solution.

Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IMAT-01 Scienza e tecnologia dei materiali

ReaCer aims to develop a new fundamental understanding of the consolidation mechanisms activated in reactive hydrothermal liquid-phase sintering, RHLPS. The main goal is to identify a kinetic model for the process and bind it to the physics of the system. This will allow us to clarify the rate-controlling bottlenecks for the reactive consolidation, the diffusion pathways, and the activation energy of the process. Remarkably, the assumptions behind this consolidation approach are mechanistically different from those mastering the traditional solid-state sintering models.
